clue.text: Pledges declined by diners who have taken the pledge

definitions.meaning: pawns, as goods left with a pawnbroker in return for a loan

definitions.text: declined by diners who have taken the pledge
definitions.meaning: teetotallers refuse German white Rhine wines at the table

explanation.surface: Diners who have sworn off alcohol turn down a round of promises.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is slang for things pawned; the second is plural of the Rhine wine, which a teetotaller (one who has taken the pledge) would refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns: items pawned with a pawnbroker, and bottles of German Rhine wine.

clue.text: Heights I'd revise if they breach the Thames barrier

indicators.note: to revise is to rework, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to amend their altitudes in case floodwater overtops London's flood defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revise' rearranges HEIGHTSID. The Thames Barrier is London's tidal flood defence, so the definition describes surges of the sea big enough to overtop it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptionally high tidal water is what would overtop a flood barrier.

clue.text: Study what the punter should study, and do likewise

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a racing punter studies the horses' form, their record of past results

explanation.surface: A betting tip: read the racing paper and copy the experts.
explanation.walkthrough: A punter is a gambler on horse races, who studies the form guide before betting.
explanation.definitionFit: To act the same way as others is to follow suit, the conventional behaviour.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A loyal backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' reads as an adjective (loyal) but is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: One stops a flow of blood; the other is the stalk holding up a plant.

clue.text: Sawyer followed by police and finally docked

parts.note: Bob Sawyer is the medical student in Dickens's Pickwick Papers
police tail a suspect, following them covertly

explanation.surface: A woodcutter is shadowed by the law and at last ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawyer' suggests a woodman or Tom Sawyer, but it is Bob Sawyer of Dickens. 'docked' means with a cut tail, not in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog or horse with its tail cut short is said to be docked.

clue.text: Starting early means rousing game before grouser appears

indicators.note: one piece placed before the other in the answer

parts.note: beaters rouse game birds from cover on a shoot
on a grouse shoot the gun is the person shooting

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly that a stirring match starts before the moaner arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouser' looks like a complainer, but it is one who shoots grouse, called a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer who leaves before the starting pistol has set off prematurely, an idiom for acting too soon.

clue.text: A word of approval for those who approve

definitions.text: A word of approval for those who approve

parts.words: A word of approval for those who approve
parts.note: an affirmative word, and in Parliament the members voting for a motion are counted under that affirmative name

explanation.surface: A word of approval is given to those who approve.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division those voting in favour are called by the old word for yes, pluralised.

clue.text: Wrongfully blacked for having begun a return to work

definitions.text: having begun a return to work

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done amiss, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A worker was unfairly boycotted for leading the strikers back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongfully' rearranges BLACKED. 'Blacked' is British trade-union slang for boycotted by strikers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have headed strikers going back to their jobs is to have guided them home again.

clue.text: Within 24 hours a theologian may be called father

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other, here the theologian inside the day

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: In a single day a churchman might be addressed as Father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' suggests a priest's title, but it is the familiar word a child uses for a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet name children use for their male parent.

clue.text: Looks after the geese?

parts.note: slang for looks, as in take a gander; also the male birds that might look after a flock of geese

explanation.surface: Someone tends the flock of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang takes a gander for a glance, and male geese might mind the flock.

clue.text: What the crockery shop is doing at Newmarket

definitions.text: What the crockery shop is doing at Newmarket

parts.words: What the crockery shop is doing at Newmarket
parts.note: a china shop sells dishes; at Newmarket racecourse a selling race offers a trophy and the winner is auctioned

explanation.surface: A china shop trades at the famous racecourse town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is England's main horse-racing town; a selling race there is one whose winner must be put up for auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A crockery shop offers dishes for sale, and minor auction races are known by the same name.

clue.text: Dead men reformed

annotationWithheld.why: Dead men reformed (7): 'reformed' must be both the anagram indicator for DEADMEN and the definition of AMENDED, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Accepted the duty of an authorising officer

definitions.text: the duty of an authorising officer
definitions.meaning: an authorising officer's job is to approve, to give things the OK

explanation.surface: An officer took on the job of signing things off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as two words, TO OK: what an authorising officer must do.
explanation.definitionFit: Received something offered; split in two it says 'to approve'.

clue.text: If all is confused wave your hands about

indicators.note: the words are muddled up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: When everything is in a muddle, people gesticulate wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is confused' rearranges IFALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash the arms around wildly, like a threshing tool swung about.

clue.text: A large number; doesn't matter which large number

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
whichever one you like

explanation.surface: A big figure, and any big figure will do.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'large number' is the Roman numeral M, a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A great quantity or a lot of something.

clue.text: Solve knotty problem when SC votes 2/2 with one abstention

parts.note: the Security Council is part of the UN, the United Nations
an equal split of votes, two for and two against, is a draw

explanation.surface: A Security Council deadlock must be broken when the votes split evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the UN Security Council; a split vote with an abstention leaves the result equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosening a knot literally, and resolving a tricky matter figuratively.

clue.text: What well-stocked debt-laden timber merchants are not out of

definitions.text: What well-stocked debt-laden timber merchants are not out of

parts.words: What well-stocked debt-laden timber merchants are not out of
parts.note: a full timber yard has plenty of trees; deep in debt they are still in trouble, not out of the forest

explanation.surface: Timber merchants with full stock and big debts are still struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not out of the ___' means still in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber and forests, with the idiom for still being in difficulty.

clue.text: A difficult task the importunate are doing at the labour exchange

definitions.text: the importunate are doing at the labour exchange
definitions.meaning: pushy jobseekers insist on being given a job at the job centre

explanation.surface: Pushy jobseekers find the job centre hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: A labour exchange is an old British name for a job centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough job, and insisting on a job from the employment office.

clue.text: Preferring the open market to the supermarket for a take-over

definitions.text: Preferring the open market to the supermarket
definitions.meaning: shopping outdoors at market stalls rather than indoors
acquiring a firm by purchasing all its shares

explanation.surface: Shopping outside the big stores is likened to a corporate acquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping outdoors, and purchasing the shares of others to take control of a company.

clue.text: Taking down job description for a laundress

definitions.meaning: a washerwoman literally handles soiled linen

explanation.surface: A laundress's work is described as humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing the dirty on' someone is a British idiom for treating them shabbily.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for treating someone shabbily, and literally washing soiled clothes.

clue.text: Dashed! The hound has done just that

definitions.meaning: a mild American oath like darned

definitions.text: The hound has done just that
definitions.meaning: the hound has dashed off, i.e. the dog has left

explanation.surface: The hound has run off, curse it!
explanation.definitionFit: A mild American curse, and split in two it says the hound has left.

clue.text: Profligates swallow pound up to get foreign notes

indicators.note: the profligates take the next piece inside them

parts.note: roués are dissolute pleasure-seekers

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for pound is read upwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Wastrels down a pound so as to obtain foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird but is the container signal; 'up' works because this is a down clue. A roué is a dissolute rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian currency units, which come as banknotes.

clue.text: Got back a Roman habit

indicators.note: the word got is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone recovered a Roman custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GOT to TOG. 'habit' means clothing, not custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment; the Roman citizen's robe was this one.

clue.text: Put on one side for greater appreciation for.

definitions.meaning: tilt or tip over so one side rises
a bigger gratuity, i.e. raising the tip

explanation.surface: Something is set aside for others to value more.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held ends with a stray 'for.', which plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilting something so it rises at one end, and raising a gratuity.

clue.text: Everyone leaves, the rest is gone!

definitions.meaning: there is no rest at all, so things are frantically busy

explanation.surface: Everybody departs and the remainder have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' suggests the remainder, but it means repose: no rest means hectic.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody departing, and the idiom for being hectically busy.

clue.text: A child of five

parts.note: not a five-year-old but one of a set born together in a multiple birth of five

explanation.surface: A five-year-old child.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for quintuplet, one of five babies born at one birth.

clue.text: … the waiting list maybe

parts.note: not a queue for treatment but the list of dishes waiters serve

explanation.surface: A hospital waiting list, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare, the list waiters work from.

clue.text: Finished!

parts.note: the umpire's call ending a set of six balls in cricket, also ending a radio message

explanation.surface: It's all done!
explanation.definitionFit: Completed, and the call ending an exchange of balls in cricket or a radio message.

clue.text: Supporting international cricket object

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A thing backing a cricket match between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection is to complain against something.

clue.text: Composer who could look to romance

indicators.note: the second piece is added to the end of the first

parts.note: a romance is a novel
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A composer who might turn to love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor, famous for 'Keep the Home Fires Burning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor of that surname was a celebrated Welsh songwriter and composer.

clue.text: Forerunner of a flash line on computer screens?

definitions.text: Forerunner of a flash line on computer screens?

parts.words: Forerunner of a flash line on computer screens?
parts.note: a forerunner, and whimsically what came before the blinking pointer line on a screen

explanation.surface: Something that preceded the blinking line on a computer display.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or harbinger; split, it is what comes before the screen pointer.

clue.text: Adjust dial readings to zero and steer another way

indicators.note: the letters of the word are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Zero the instruments and change course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another way' rearranges STEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a gauge to its starting value of nothing.
